title: Multiplayer: world actions do not synchronize between clients

path.to: Live online match (STDB host, --db or --pN): the local player places and breaks blocks while a second identity watches the same match

java: Run the pinned server (./gradlew server:run, then `host`), join two desktop clients at 127.0.0.1:6567.

Client A places a conveyor/drill: client B's world shows the same block at the same tile; the tile mutation travels as the Tile.setTile @Remote (Tile.java:386-396, Tile.java:848) and the server applies/rebroadcasts it.
Client A breaks the block: B sees the removal (Call.removeTile, Tile.java:386).
godot: Start an online client (godot --path client -- --db); host a match via MindNet.create_match (or the paused Host dialog) and drive the session to in_lobby/in_game.
Place a block with the normal input path (left click on the world, GUI not consumed; MindSimHost.unhandled_input -> apply_command, sim_host.rs:186-191).

Read MindNet.last_applied_command_id()/relay_queue_depth() and `spacetime sql mindustry "SELECT command_id,kind FROM match_command ORDER BY command_id DESC LIMIT 3"`: the local sim changed but no match_command row for the local action exists.

On a second identity in the match read get_state_json(): the tile is unchanged; a foreign send_command_json({"op":"place","block":"conveyor"}) is ignored because relay.rs kind_to_sim only maps PlaceBlock/BreakBlock and block_id only resolves "router".
compare: Java: every world mutation made by a client is sent to the server and rebroadcast, so both clients converge. Godot: the shipped input path never calls MindNet.send_command_json/emit_command, so nothing is published; and the inbound mapping drops every CommandKind except PlaceBlock/BreakBlock, with any non-router block name resolving to block id 0.

plan.state: seeded by code-scan 2026-10-10; not yet verified in-engine
plan.seam: client/rust/mind-gdext/src/sim_host.rs:186-191 applies local place/break directly into Sim::apply with no relay hand-off; the only publication seam client/rust/mind-gdext/src/net/mod.rs:740 (MindNet.emit_command, via send_command_json:443) has no shipped caller, and the inbound mapping client/rust/mind-gdext/src/net/relay.rs:22 is a stub.
plan.approach: 1) Give MindSimHost a relay-publish hook: on an accepted local Place/Break (sim_host.rs:186-191) it resolves the selected block's content NAME and forwards (x,y,block name,rotation) to MindNet, which sends it through CommandSender::send (net/mod.rs:740) instead of only applying locally; keep the local apply as the prediction and let the own-echo skip (relay.rs:111) drop the duplicate. 2) Replace the relay.rs:43 1-name block mirror with the live ContentRegistry name->id lookup so foreign blocks resolve to the real id (currently only "router" -> 1, everything else -> 0). 3) Expand RelayRuntime::kind_to_sim (relay.rs:22-39) to the full CommandKind set that affects the sim (ConfigBlock, Rotate, UnitCommand/UnitStance/UnitCommandQueue, PlayerSpawn, SetRule/SetRules, SkipWave/RunWave, AdminSwitchTeam, LogicSync, ...), mapping to canonical SimCommand at tick boundaries. 4) Add a two-client scenario/golden so the published row and the applied state are asserted.
plan.narrow_check: Two-client live check: A places a conveyor while B watches; `spacetime sql mindustry "SELECT kind FROM match_command ORDER BY command_id DESC LIMIT 1"` returns the PlaceBlock row and B's SimHost.get_state_json() shows the same tile; then A sends MindNet.send_command_json({"op":"place","x":..,"y":..,"block":"conveyor"}) and B applies conveyor (not air). A headless two-client relay scenario can assert the same without a window.

note: Code-scan 2026-10-10 (multiplayer): S2, high confidence. Player impact: in a live match nothing the player does is published - the relay log stays empty, remote clients see a frozen world, and foreign non-place/break actions (configs, rotation, unit orders, rules, waves, team switch) are silently dropped. Context: the outbound half and the inbound stub are the same seam (the relay is receive-only for the shipped input path); block configs also arrive as air because block_id only knows "router". In-engine verification pending.

title: Multiplayer: in-game chat is inert (sent messages reach nobody, incoming messages never render; /t, /a and /votekick have no handler)

path.to: Live online match: press Enter / submit a message in the chat fragment, then send one from a second identity

java: Java server + two clients in a match: client A presses Enter (ChatFragment.java:63-66 toggles when net.active()), types hi and submits.
Client B's chat log shows hi is broadcast; the server path is the NetClient.sendChatMessage @Remote (NetClient.java:333) and the peer render is ChatFragment.addMessage.
B types /votekick <A> reason and /vote y: the server vote session replies (NetServer.java:394-475, gated by Config.enableVotekick, Administration.java:539).
godot: Open a live match and call get_node("/root/MindUi").chat_send("hello","normal") (or submit in the chat fragment): it returns true but only re-emits the local chat_message signal (ui_host.rs:533-542); nothing listens and no reducer runs.
Check `spacetime sql mindustry "SELECT chat_id,text FROM match_chat ORDER BY chat_id DESC LIMIT 3"`: no row from the UI path (MindNet.send_chat, net/mod.rs:592, has no caller at all).

Insert a row as the peer (second client or reducer call) and re-read the chat fragment log: add_message is never invoked because MindNet never binds my_match_chat (attach_binders, net/mod.rs:222-234; the table is in GAME_TABLES, waves.rs:43).

Press Enter in game: the "chat" binding (binding.rs:775) falls through the desktop bridge `_ => {}` (desktop.rs:599), so the fragment is not even opened. enableVotekick exists only as a config spec (config.rs:106-108) and PlayerAction::Vote only fails (player_list.rs:26,151-163).
compare: Java: chat toggles on Enter while net.active(), travels to the server, is filtered/broadcast and rendered in every peer's ChatFragment; /t, /a and /votekick are server-parsed client commands. Godot: the chat fragment is unreachable from input, submit is a local-only signal, MindNet.send_chat has no caller, and no my_match_chat binder feeds add_message - chat and its command surface (including vote-kick) are fully inert.

plan.state: seeded by code-scan 2026-10-10; not yet verified in-engine
plan.seam: client/rust/mind-gdext/src/ui/ui_host.rs:533-542 (chat_send emits a signal only) has no consumer; client/rust/mind-gdext/src/net/mod.rs:592 (MindNet.send_chat) and the my_match_chat table (waves.rs:43) are never wired; the chat/player_list input bindings die at client/rust/mind-gdext/src/input/desktop.rs:599.
plan.approach: 1) Route the fragment submit to the relay: connect the chat fragment's send to /root/Spine/MindNet.send_chat (or have MindUi hold a MindNet handle) and map the fragment mode to ChatKind (normal->All, team->Team, admin->System/admin check); keep the local buffer as echo. 2) Bind MyMatchChatTableAccessor in MindNet.attach_binders (net/mod.rs:222), drain rows and forward sender/kind/text to the chat fragment's add_message with the same rolling-log behaviour. 3) Handle the "chat" binding in the desktop bridge to toggle the fragment and set FocusState.chat_shown (same for "player_list" if not covered by the player-list finding). 4) Parse `/`-commands server-side or in a client command dispatcher; for vote-kick add the upstream session (NetServer.java:394-475): >=3 players, enableVotekick gate, target checks, vote/cooldown, cancel-by-admin, kick on pass, and a player-list vote button. 5) Only then decide the per-match chat-filter scope (chat-filter finding).
plan.narrow_check: Live match: submit through the chat fragment -> `spacetime sql mindustry "SELECT text FROM match_chat ORDER BY chat_id DESC LIMIT 1"` shows the sanitized row for the sender identity, and a second identity's chat fragment _log contains it. A chat-command unit/headless test covers /votekick -> session -> kick path with enableVotekick on/off.

title: Multiplayer: the player list is always empty and its kick/ban/trace/team actions cannot execute; Admins/Bans dialogs always show 'none'

path.to: Live match with two members (host/admin + peer): open the player list (Tab) or call MindUi.player_list_json/player_action; open the Admins/Bans dialogs

java: Java server + two clients; client A is admin/host; press Tab (Binding.playerList, DesktopInput.java:233) to open the player list.

Click the peer row menu: Ban/Kick/Trace/Team/Admin buttons are present (PlayerListFragment.java:149-247); Kick sends AdminAction.kick via Call.adminRequest and the peer disconnects; Trace opens TraceDialog from the traceInfo reply (NetClient.java:415).
Press @server.bans / @server.admins: the dialogs list netServer.admins data (AdminsDialog.java:32-49, BansDialog.java:32-50) and unadmin/unban work.
godot: In a live match call get_node("/root/MindUi").player_list_json(): it is hard-coded "[]" (ui_host.rs:559) even though MindNet.get_members_json() has rows; the fragment therefore renders only @players.notfound (player_list_fragment.gd:53-72).

Call MindUi.player_action("peer","kick"): always false (ui_host.rs:547-554); PlayerListModel::dispatch also returns RelayUnavailable (player_list.rs:151-163), so no admin reducer (Connector::admin_kick/admin_ban/admin_switch_team, connector.rs:824-934) is ever sent and `spacetime sql mindustry "SELECT action FROM admin_action_log ..."` stays empty.

Press Tab: the player_list binding (binding.rs:769) falls through `_ => {}` (desktop.rs:599) - there is no live toggle; a kicked peer also never sees my_kick (waves.rs:37, never bound in net/mod.rs:222-234).

title: Multiplayer: joining a running match does not sync the world (no late-join map load or snapshot catch-up)

path.to: Second client joins a match that is already Running (host created + started the match, then the joiner calls MindNet.join_match)

java: Java server + client A start and play a match; connect client B afterwards.

B runs the connect handshake and the server sends the world (NetServer.requestWorld -> sendWorldData, NetServer.java:955-959, WorldReloader) plus the state snapshot, so B is in sync with A's tiles, units and wave state.
godot: Client A hosts (create_match) and starts the match; client B joins with MindNet.join_match(id, "").

On B read session_state()/get_match_state_json() plus SimHost.get_tick()/get_checksum(): B reaches in_game but nothing loads the match's map/seed (join_match only drives the session state machine, net/mod.rs:338-367; drain_match_rows only mirrors JSON, net/mod.rs:662-684).

Read MindNet.snapshot_progress() and `spacetime sql mindustry "SELECT snapshot_id FROM match_snapshot"`: progress stays 0 and no snapshot request happens; request_snapshot is only triggered on an in-game desync (net/mod.rs:798-801).

Force the request path (MindNet.request_snapshot()): the Snapshot wave is subscribed but no my_match_snapshot_chunks binder exists (attach_binders, net/mod.rs:222-234) and SnapshotProgress/reassemble have no live caller (snapshot.rs:296/517; SaveIo::load_bytes is used only for campaign map files, sim_host.rs:1798), so the blob is never reassembled or applied.
compare: Java: a late joiner receives the world/state stream and converges to the host. Godot: joining a Running match only flips SessionState; the joiner keeps its own unrelated sim, no snapshot is requested/reassembled/applied and the command tail after the snapshot watermark is not replayed (plans/21_MULTIPLAYER_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md:447 still lists the late-join sequence unchecked).

plan.state: seeded by code-scan 2026-10-10; not yet verified in-engine
plan.seam: client/rust/mind-gdext/src/net/mod.rs:338-367 (join_match) never loads the match map nor runs a late-join sequence; request_snapshot fires only on desync (net/mod.rs:798-801), my_match_snapshot_chunks is never bound (net/mod.rs:222-234) and nothing applies a reassembled snapshot to the sim.
plan.approach: 1) Add the late-join sequence on observe_match with status Running (and after Resync/reconnect): subscribe the Snapshot wave, bind my_match_snapshot_chunks, call request_snapshot and feed rows into SnapshotProgress/reassemble (mind-stdb helpers already exist). 2) Apply the reassembled blob through the plan-04 entity/save codec into the live sim (Sim/sim_host need a net restore entry; today SaveIo::load_bytes serves only campaign preset maps, sim_host.rs:1798) after regenerating terrain from header.map_id/map_seed and applying header.rules_json/wave state. 3) Replay the ordered command tail after header.command_id (CommandRing::tail_after) and only then exit_snapshot_sync. 4) Make reconnect follow the same path when the member row survives and the match is still Running (plans/21 section 3.8 line 241).
plan.narrow_check: Two-client live check: B joins a Running match; MindNet.snapshot_progress() reaches 1.0, session_state() goes snapshot_sync -> in_game, and B's scoped checksum/tile state equal A's after the tail replay. A headless mp_late_join scenario (fixture snapshot + tail) asserts reassembly and watermark ordering without a window.

note: Code-scan 2026-10-10 (multiplayer): S2, high confidence. Player impact: a player joining a match already in progress never receives the host's world/state, so their sim diverges immediately and no snapshot correction is possible (the request path exists but the chunks are never consumed or applied). Context: plans/21:447 still lists 'late-join sequence; reconnect path' as open and plans/24:190 lists the live late-join timing as deferred; reconnect shares the same missing catch-up. In-engine verification pending.

title: Dedicated server: the host command never creates a networked match, so no client can join and kick/say/runwave do nothing

path.to: mind-headless serve (or server) boot, console `host <map> <mode>` then `status`, `kick <name>`, `runwave`, and a client looking at all_matches

java: Run ./gradlew server:run; enter `host <map> survival`: ServerControl.java:512-563 loads the map and calls netServer.openServer() (ServerControl.java:560, NetServer.java:1083), so the server is listed/joinable and kick/say act on connected players.
godot: Boot the dedicated shape: `cargo run --manifest-path client/rust/Cargo.toml -p mind-headless -- serve --config-dir /tmp/mgsrv --stdb-host http://127.0.0.1:3000` (serve composes `host <map> <mode>` at dedicated.rs:193-198) or `... server`; then send `host synthetic survival`.

Send `status` and `players`: the console host command went through LocalHost (commands.rs:381), so the report is the local synthetic fixture with 0 players; `spacetime sql mindustry "SELECT match_id,map_id,status FROM relay_match"` returns no row because NetHost::host (net_host.rs:277-302, the create_match path) is never called.

Send `kick <name>` / `say hi` / `runwave`: kick and say go to state.net (commands.rs:466/435) whose session has no match, so they fail with 'no match is hosted' (or act offline-mirror-only), and runwave increments the local fixture wave (commands.rs:775-780 -> host.rs:351-355) instead of emitting admin_run_wave (net_host.rs:324-335).
compare: Java: `host` opens the real server (openServer) and all console admin verbs act on the live connection. Godot: ServerState keeps LocalHost for host/stop/status/runwave and NetHost only for admin verbs, so the STDB match is never created - the server is invisible in all_matches, no client can join, and kick/say cannot target anyone.

plan.state: seeded by code-scan 2026-10-10; not yet verified in-engine
plan.seam: client/rust/mind-headless/src/server/commands.rs:378-385 (cmd_host -> state.host.host, LocalHost) never calls NetHost::host (client/rust/mind-headless/src/server/net_host.rs:277-302), so the STDB session has no match; stop/status/runwave are split the same way (commands.rs:290, 775).
plan.approach: 1) Make the console `host` drive the networked host: keep the LocalHost fixture only for offline mode and call NetHost::host (net_host.rs:277) when online, so create_match runs and the Lobby/Game waves are subscribed. 2) Route `stop` to NetHost::stop (leave_match) and `runwave` to NetHost::run_wave (admin_run_wave, net_host.rs:324) whenever a networked match is hosted (LocalHost stays for the offline fixture). 3) Report NetHost status/players in `status` and keep `players`/kick/say on state.net. 4) Feed the parsed --match-config (map/seed/visibility/max_players) into HostParams instead of the defaults, and wire the serve auto-pause/rotation decisions (dedicated.rs should_pause/next_map currently have no caller). 5) Exercise it in the MIND_STDB_IT two-peer integration test.
plan.narrow_check: `serve` + `host synthetic survival` against a local SpacetimeDB: `spacetime sql mindustry "SELECT match_id,map_id,status FROM relay_match"` returns one Lobby/Running row, a Godot client's Join/Global list shows it and can join, and `kick <name>` returns success against the live member row instead of 'no match is hosted'.

note: Code-scan 2026-10-10 (multiplayer): S2, high confidence. Player impact: the dedicated-server flow cannot host - no match row exists, so the server never appears in the browser, nobody can join, and the admin console verbs (kick/say/players/runwave) act on nothing or on a local synthetic fixture. Context: lead 2 (server console admin reachability); NetHost::host is dead code and the serve path reuses the local command. In-engine verification pending.

title: Chat filters/mutes are database-global and apply to every match on the SpacetimeDB database, not per match

path.to: One SpacetimeDB database hosting two concurrent matches; an admin adds a mute filter from one match and a player posts the pattern in the other

java: Java is one server = one match, so Administration.chatFilters (Administration.java:28) applies only to that server's players via filterMessage (Administration.java:153-160, applied in NetClient.java:364 and NetServer.java:374): a filter added by the server admin affects exactly the live match.
godot: Create two matches in the same database (or reason from the schema): chat_filter/chat_rate have no match_id (chat/mod.rs:29-81), so send_chat loads every filter row for whichever match is calling (chat/mod.rs:128-143) and a mute pattern added for match A drops the same text in match B.

Check the management surface too: no client or console caller invokes Connector::admin_add_chat_filter/admin_remove_chat_filter (connector.rs:889-905) - there is currently no UI/console way to manage filters at all.
compare: Upstream: filters are server-global which equals per-match (one match per server); the message path is filterMessage before broadcast. Godot: the filter/mute table is shared by every match in the database, and with no management surface the admin cannot scope or even edit filters. plans/24:192 records this as an accepted deviation awaiting the authoritative sim - keep open, do not mark wontfix.

plan.state: seeded by code-scan 2026-10-10; not yet verified in-engine
